title: Asking for structured output when it makes consumption easier

videos.script: In this course, a program reads the answer next, not a person. That is the only reason to ask for JSON. {{title}} The same message, answered in prose, is fine for somebody on the support team. A router needs a field it can find by name, and a value it can compare. {{prose}} Structure has a price. The prompt grows, and every brace and quote is a token the model writes. {{cost}} Then comes the contract. The checks in the lab are a schema in miniature: which keys must be there, which ones may be, and what values each one takes. {{checks}} One line in the prompt, asking for nothing around the JSON, takes the replies that parse from twenty-seven to thirty-seven. {{strict}} A lenient parser would hide that. Under it the two prompts score the same, and the improvement disappears. {{lenient}} And three replies in forty still do not parse. You decide what the program does with them: try again, fall back, or hand them to a person. It never guesses. {{close}}
